title: Derivatives and fixed income for analysts
objectives: Explain futures and options payoffs and the bond price-yield link.
Use derivatives data as a research input.
body_md:
Analysts meet derivatives and bonds even in an equity role.

## Futures and options

- A **future** is an obligation to buy or sell at a set price on a date.
- An **option** is a right, not an obligation. A **call** gives the right to buy; a **put** the right to sell. The buyer's maximum loss is the **premium**.
- **Open interest** and the **put-call ratio** hint at positioning.
- **Options Greeks:** delta (price sensitivity), theta (time decay), vega (volatility).
- Single-stock derivatives in India are physically settled; index derivatives are cash settled (verify current rules).

## Bonds

| Concept | Rule |
|---|---|
| Price and yield | Move in **opposite** directions |
| Duration | Measures sensitivity to rate changes; longer duration, bigger swings |
| Credit spread | Extra yield for default risk |
| Yield curve | Yields across maturities; inversion can signal slowdown |

> **Exam tip:** Remember that the option buyer's loss is capped at the premium, while the seller's can be large.
example: A bond yielding 7% rises in price when market yields fall to 6.5%. A bond fund with long duration gains more than one with short duration.
